problems.description: Session 1 collapses the seed's deliberate model/route separation: create_task, get_tasks, update_task, and the fetch_task alias are deleted and their SQL inlined directly into route handlers. The baseline was explicitly designed with 'good seams' for multi-session stories; this removes the model layer future sessions are supposed to build on and couples data access to the HTTP layer.

Deletes documented backward-compat surface (_legacy_format_date, _notify_admin, fetch_task) that the seed intentionally retained ('retained for backward compatibility', 'not yet wired'). Removing them erases the story's seeded seams and can break legacy clients that the app was written to keep working.
init_db() now executes at module import time (side effect on import) rather than only under __main__; harmless while idempotent, but it couples app.py to filesystem state on import.

Discrepancy: the mechanical convention score (0.64, 10 violations) is repo-wide and dominated by violations in files untouched by this commit (celery_config.py, notification_tasks.py, repositories.py). The two app.py flags are static-analysis false positives — app.py defines no classes (PascalCase N/A) and the module-level constant was actually relocated into app.config, removing the UPPER_CASE violation. Commit-level conventions are improved (type hints, docstrings, snake_case).

strengths: Adds a real pytest suite (test_app.py) with a tmp_path-isolated DATABASE fixture that calls init_db() explicitly.
Moves DATABASE into app.config, improving testability and removing the module-level constant flag.
Adds proper input validation (validate_title, isinstance checks), rowcount-based 404 on UPDATE, and fixes the seed's create bug by letting status default to 'pending' instead of hardcoding 'done'.
All SQL remains parameterized (no injection surface); uses timezone-aware UTC timestamps; net -2 SonarQube smells.
commit_reviews.summary: A well-tested, validation-hardened rewrite that fixes real defects, but it flattens the seed's model/route architecture and deletes the documented legacy stubs, erasing exactly the seams the multi-session story was engineered to measure.

problems.description: Hand-rolled JWT (encode/decode via base64+hmac) instead of a battle-tested library like PyJWT; subtle spec gaps (e.g. no alg confusion guard, lenient base64 padding) are easy to get wrong. HMAC is implemented correctly with compare_digest, but custom crypto is avoidable tech debt.
JWT_SECRET falls back to a hardcoded 'development-secret-change-me'; if deployed without the env var set, all tokens are forgeable.
JWT_EXPIRATION_HOURS default of 24 with no refresh/revocation path; token invalidation on password change or logout is impossible with a purely stateless HS256 scheme.

Convention score 0.64 reflects violations largely in files outside this commit's hunks (celery_config.py, notification_tasks.py, repositories.py) plus 'Classes should use PascalCase' in app.py that does not match the snake_case functions this diff adds — likely pre-existing or false-positive linter findings, not introduced here.

strengths: Data-preserving migration: nullable owner_id via ALTER TABLE keeps pre-auth task records valid and the init_db migration logic is idempotent.
Constant-time signature verification via hmac.compare_digest and a shared signing-input builder between encode/decode.
Strong adherence to existing codebase patterns: same get_db()/dict(row) style, plain SQLite, validate_* helpers, route naming, and JSON error shape with correct status codes (400/401/404/409).
Ownership scoping consistently applied across create/list/show/update so multi-user data stays isolated.
commit_reviews.summary: A well-patterned, data-safe authentication layer that fits the existing architecture cleanly, but hand-rolling JWTs (plus a lax default secret) introduces avoidable security/maintainability debt.

problems.description: Fabricates a fallback email (f"{username}@example.com") when the user has no email, so a notification is sent to a made-up address instead of requiring or skipping it; this is a data-integrity hack that would misfire in production.
Cognitive complexity +9 in update_task (nested completion check + ternary); the completion-notification logic could be extracted into a helper to keep the handler lean.
No test covers the no-email fallback branch; the fabricated-email path (existing_task["email"] or username@example.com) is untested.

Convention score 0.64 with 10 violations, mostly module-level constant casing in celery_config.py/notification_tasks.py and repositories.py; several are false positives since Celery's config_from_object requires lowercase keys (broker_url, result_backend, task_routes) and celery_app is a standard idiom.

strengths: Enqueues the notification only after the DB write commits (outside the with get_db() block), so failed transactions never emit notifications.
Re-completion deduplication is handled via the status transition check and covered by a dedicated test.
Fully-qualified task name (notification_tasks.send_notification_email) matches the task_routes queue mapping.
DB migration respects existing installations via PRAGMA table_info + ALTER TABLE, mirroring the owner_id migration pattern.
Extends existing conventions cleanly (validate_credentials 3-tuple, get_db(), jsonify error style) and adds targeted tests.
commit_reviews.summary: Solid Celery integration that enqueues after commit, dedups re-completions, and adds tests, though the fabricated username@example.com fallback is a maintainability wart and the convention violations are largely false positives on Celery-required lowercase config names.

problems.description: Refactor touches auth-sensitive paths (register, login, update_task) and adds +167/-85 lines plus a new 140-line module, but no test file changes appear in the diff; the repository layer and refactored endpoints ship without test coverage.

update_task now reads via get_notification_details and writes via update_for_owner in two separate connections, losing the single-transaction read-modify-write guarantee the original 'with get_db()' block provided (small TOCTOU window).
Refactor is partial: app.py keeps get_db/init_db while schema DDL lives in repositories.initialize_database, splitting schema ownership across two modules.

Most measured convention violations (celery_config.py, notification_tasks.py) are in files untouched by this diff; the ones touching this commit's files (module-level 'task_repository'/'user_repository' instances and the 'ConnectionFactory' type alias flagged as UPPER_CASE constants) appear to be false positives from a naive linter.

strengths: Introduces a clean repository layer (BaseRepository ABC + TaskRepository/UserRepository) that centralizes data access and removes duplicated inline SQL from route handlers.
Keeps the existing get_db context-manager idiom and applies consistent type hints, docstrings, PascalCase classes, and snake_case methods in the new code.
Net static-quality improvement: bugs +0, smells -1, duplications +0.0%, and +167/-85 lines is a favorable extraction ratio.
commit_reviews.summary: A solid architectural refactor that cleanly extracts data access into a typed repository layer and reduces duplication, with the main concerns being no added test coverage and a minor loss of transaction atomicity in update_task.

problems.description: RATELIMIT_STORAGE_URI defaults to redis://localhost:6379/0, introducing a hard runtime Redis dependency the app did not have; rate-limited endpoints will fail if Redis is unavailable.

Test fixture mutates private library internals (limiter._storage / limiter._limiter); the RATELIMIT_STORAGE_URI='memory://' config is ineffective because Limiter is bound to app at import time, making the override a workaround.
list_for_owner is now dead code in repositories.py — its only caller was replaced by list_page_for_owner but the method was not removed.
require_auth now depends on g.authenticated_user_id being set by the before_request hook; removing or reordering the hook silently breaks auth with an AttributeError instead of a clean 401.
before_request decodes the JWT on every request, including anonymous requests that only need the client IP for rate-limit keying.
/tasks response shape changed from a bare list to {data, next_cursor, total} — a breaking API contract change, though tests were updated in lockstep within this story.

strengths: Keyset pagination with a (created_at, id) tiebreaker gives stable ordering and bounded page queries; the tiebreaker also fixes determinism in the existing list_for_owner sort.
Rate limiting keyed by authenticated user id with IP fallback, plus a 429 handler that sets Retry-After, is security-conscious.
Pagination and count logic live in the repository layer, keeping the route thin and consistent with the existing architecture.
New code adheres to the project's snake_case functions, type hints, and docstring conventions; the +6 imports are targeted.
Tests were updated in lockstep with the response-contract change, keeping the suite green.
commit_reviews.summary: A well-contained cross-cutting commit adding rate limiting and keyset pagination that respects the existing decorator/repository layering; minor debt from a hard Redis default and import-time limiter binding, and the mechanical 0.64 convention score reflects pre-existing repo-wide violations (celery_config.py, notification_tasks.py) rather than anything this diff introduces.

compounding_issues: Hand-rolled HS256 JWT in Session 2 (no PyJWT) with a hardcoded, non-rotating default secret ('development-secret-change-me') carried to the end — functionally sound but a lingering security smell
Nullable owner_id migration in Session 2 leaves pre-auth rows with NULL owner_id that no user can ever access — deliberate data-preservation tradeoff that creates permanently orphaned tasks
Session 3 (Celery) and Session 5 (Flask-Limiter) both default to Redis at redis://localhost:6379/0, silently making the whole API depend on a running Redis instance in production
Seed's create_task bug (persists 'done', returns 'pending') plus unused legacy helpers forced Session 1 into a near-total rewrite rather than an incremental fix
key_decisions: Session 2: standard-library HS256 JWT + Werkzeug password hashing, avoiding an auth dependency while keeping signatures correct (compare_digest, exp checks)
Session 2: nullable owner_id ALTER TABLE migration to preserve legacy task rows while scoping all reads/writes to the authenticated owner

Session 3: Celery/Redis async email notifications enqueued only on status transition into 'completed' (idempotent completion), with a deterministic <username>@example.com fallback for users without email
Session 4: extraction of BaseRepository/TaskRepository/UserRepository behind a connection-factory seam — a behavior-preserving refactor that Session 5's keyset pagination then extends
Session 5: per-authenticated-user rate limiting keyed off a before_request identity hook (single token decode reused by require_auth) plus (created_at, id) keyset cursor pagination
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved monotonically. Test coverage grew 8 -> 13 -> 15 -> 15 -> 21 with every commit green, following a classic incremental arc: Session 1 repaired the buggy seed (wrong status persistence, lazy schema init) into a consistent CRUD API; Session 2 layered authentication and ownership scoping on a forward-compatible migration; Session 3 integrated asynchronous notifications with idempotency; Session 4 flattened the architecture into a clean repository layer without behavioral drift (the one deliberately flat checkpoint, same 15 tests); and Session 5 exploited that seam to add cross-cutting rate limiting and cursor pagination. The agent consistently reasoned about compatibility with earlier decisions (reusing the S2 token scheme, the S4 repositories, the S3 email fallback) and validated each session with the full suite.
story_review.summary: A highly coherent, steadily-improving five-session build that layered auth, notifications, a repository refactor, and cross-cutting rate-limiting/pagination on a repaired baseline, with only minor cumulative tech debt (hardcoded JWT secret, growing Redis coupling, orphaned pre-auth rows).
